assigned.title: Install, upgrade, uninstall, reinstall — tested, not assumed
assigned.acceptance: The installer's lifecycle is exercised automatically wherever that is possible on a runner, and everything that is not is named for the commander's machine. REQUIRED: clean install on a machine that has never had the application, then launch. REQUIRED: upgrade over a previous version with user data preserved, which is the one a release breaks most often and nobody tests. REQUIRED: uninstall leaves no service, no scheduled task and no orphaned node.exe, and states exactly what user data it keeps or removes. REQUIRED: reinstall after uninstall. REQUIRED: each case is marked automated or commander-machine, with the reason, so the split is visible rather than implied.
assigned.notes: PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect RULING, round 80. Created unowned as part of the WINDOWS PRODUCT COMPLETION phase board so the proposal is machine-readable rather than prose, and NOT claimed before the verdict. SURFACE NOTE: this task's allowedPaths name directories that do not exist yet. The evidence-based narrowing procedure applies to reconciling work already in history; for genuinely new work the surface is the smallest set of paths the acceptance can be satisfied within, and it is narrowed again from the diff before review if it turns out to be wider than what was written.

unit.evidence:
node --test scripts/windows/test-lifecycle.mjs: 32 tests, 32 pass, 0 fail -- the platform-independent half of the harness (the section-F plan parser, the installed-identity derivation, the residue classifier, and the harness own refusal to run off win32). scripts/windows/lifecycle.mjs --plan exits 0 and enumerates F1-F6 with owners.

This gate is unchanged in substance from the round-112 audit; ai:unblock discarded it and it is re-recorded. The evidence that CHANGED is in the build gate.

build.evidence:
WINDOWS PACKAGE #18 (run 37259195413, head 5e96f30) EXERCISED THE HARNESS ON A REAL WINDOWS RUNNER. This is the evidence this task has been blocked on since round 112, and it is the first F1-F4 result in the project history. package job: SUCCESS, 6m 26s -- also a first.

QUOTED FROM THE JOB ANNOTATIONS, not inferred from a badge:
  "Automated section-F cases on this runner: not-run=1 pass=3. These rows GATE the build: a fail fails the job."
  F1 - PASS - Clean install, then launch [owner AUTO+RIG], install command status 0
  F2 - NOT-RUN - Upgrade over a previous version [owner AUTO], "no --previous-msi was supplied"
  F3 - PASS - Uninstall [owner AUTO+RIG], msiexec uninstall status 0
  F4 - PASS - Reinstall after uninstall [owner AUTO], status 0

AGAINST THE FIVE REQUIRED CLAUSES, one at a time.
(1) "clean install on a machine that has never had the application, then launch" -- the automated half PASSES: msiexec /i status 0 followed by verifyInstalledTree. The LAUNCH half is RIG by the harness own plan ("automatedPortion: install and verify the installed tree; manualPortion: launching the application and seeing a window") and is named as such in the annotation owner tag, which is clause 5 working.
(2) "upgrade over a previous version with user data preserved" -- NOT-RUN, with the reason. This is the clause the directive forbids faking, and the harness refuses to: an upgrade needs a previous version to upgrade FROM and this repository has never shipped one. Recorded as not-run rather than pass or fail, because nothing about the product failed. It stays outstanding for PW-0505 and needs a genuine previous-release artifact, which is an external boundary.
(3) "uninstall leaves no service, no scheduled task and no orphaned node.exe, and states exactly what user data it keeps" -- F3 PASS, and the pass is load-bearing: the harness records F3 as pass ONLY when msiexec /x returns 0 AND classifyResidue(observe(where), identity).clean is true, which checks services by binary path and by product name, scheduled tasks, and processes. A dirty residue is recorded as FAIL.
(4) "reinstall after uninstall" -- F4 PASS, and it is also only recorded pass when verifyInstalledTree returns 0 afterwards, so the reinstalled tree was verified rather than assumed.
(5) "each case is marked automated or commander-machine, with the reason" -- the annotations carry [owner AUTO] and [owner AUTO+RIG] per row and the not-run reason verbatim.

A SECOND RESULT WORTH NAMING, because it is evidence PW-0208 has been waiting on and it arrived here. F1 and F4 both pass through verifyInstalledTree, which is scripts/windows/verify-install.mjs -- the check PL-0729 extended to require THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md present AND NON-EMPTY. It returned 0 TWICE against a real installed tree on a real Windows machine. So the notices file is present and non-empty in the INSTALLED TREE, which is a different tree from the package build output and from source intent, and is the strongest form of that evidence.

WHAT THIS STILL DOES NOT SHOW: what is inside the installers. The package job succeeded so upload-installers ran, but a GitHub artifact needs a login this session does not have, and a successful run produces no step-trail annotation to read an inventory from. PL-0737 built the inventory for exactly this and PL-0738 wires it in; until then the CONTENTS of the MSI remain unobserved from here.

assigned.title: The commander's run sheet, and the evidence it produces
assigned.acceptance: The commander can run the real-device half in one sitting and hand back evidence that is worth recording. REQUIRED: an ordered run sheet with a stated environment -- Windows build, GPU, driver, display, audio device -- because a pass on unrecorded hardware is not reproducible evidence. REQUIRED: for each row, the exact action, the expected result, and what to capture when it fails. REQUIRED: a defect report format that carries enough to reproduce: the reason trail the player already publishes, the log location PW-0501 establishes, and the version PW-0502 exposes. REQUIRED: the sheet is honest about how long it takes. THE RUN ITSELF IS A LAST_MILE ITEM and this task delivers the sheet, not the results; recording a pass nobody observed would be fabricating a gate result.

assigned.title: A standing check for a test that is skipped in every configuration this repository runs
assigned.acceptance:
THIS REPOSITORY HAS FOUND THE SAME DEFECT FOUR TIMES AND EACH TIME BY ACCIDENT. A thing exists, it passes, and no gate asks it: scripts/test-validate-repo.mjs until PL-AI-0002; scripts/test-desktop-target.mjs and the 30-case Windows lifecycle suite until PL-0714; components/player/tracks.ts until PW-0306; and the three fail-closed e2e titles until PL-0717, which found them by running two suites to completion and intersecting their skip lists by hand.

REQUIRED: that intersection is computed by a script rather than by somebody remembering to think of it. It reads the JSON reports the e2e job produces for each configuration and reports every test skipped in ALL of them.
REQUIRED: an ALLOWLIST of rows that legitimately run nowhere, declared and reasoned. Today it is exactly two, both media-rig rows, which need hardware no CI runner has. A row that must stay uncovered is a decision somebody records; a row that DRIFTS into being uncovered is a defect, and the allowlist is what distinguishes them.
REQUIRED: the check FAILS the build on an unlisted row. A warning inside a passing pipeline is how all four of the originals survived every gate this repository runs -- validate-workspace-deps.mjs says exactly that about itself and is right.
REQUIRED: non-vacuity. The check must be shown to FAIL against the reports as they were BEFORE PL-0717 -- where the three fail-closed titles were skipped in both configurations -- not merely to pass against today's.
REQUIRED: it runs somewhere a gate asks it, which means `npm run test:scripts` and therefore package.json. A check for things nothing runs that nothing runs would be the joke it sounds like.

OUT OF SCOPE: deciding whether any particular row SHOULD be covered. The check reports and refuses; what to do about a row it names is the owning task's judgement.
assigned.notes: FILED ROUND 111 by claude-test while implementing PL-0717, whose own notes proposed it. Filed rather than folded in, because PL-0717's surface is .github/workflows/ci.yml alone and this needs a script file plus package.json. BACKLOG rather than READY: it depends on PL-0717, which is what first made a configuration write a JSON report at all, and the check wants one from every configuration.\n\nThe allowedPaths entries are provisional -- the implementer should settle the script's home (scripts/ beside its siblings looks right) and correct them deliberately before starting.

unit.evidence: node --test scripts/assert-no-row-runs-nowhere.test.mjs: 14 tests, 14 pass, 0 fail. NON-VACUITY IS THE CENTRAL CASE AND IT IS DRIVEN TWICE, once on fixtures and once on real reports. (a) The case named "NON-VACUITY: it fails against the reports as they were before PL-0717" builds the two-configuration shape this repository had before PL-0717, with the three fail-closed titles skipped in both, and asserts exit 1 naming all three -- and asserts the two allowlisted media-rig rows are NOT named. A companion case adds the third configuration and the identical reports go green, so the check is not simply hostile to those titles. (b) Against REAL Playwright JSON reports produced locally this round from all three configurations (production+PostgreSQL 51 skipped, development 31 skipped, production-no-database 82 skipped, 153 rows each): three reports gives exit 0, excusing exactly the two media-rig rows; the same two pre-PL-0717 reports alone gives exit 1 naming exactly the three fail-closed titles PL-0717 found by hand. The allowlist is baked into the script with no override flag, so the tests use the real media-rig identities. CI WIRING VERIFIED LOCALLY: PL-0714 mirror-check, extracted from the workflow and run here, reports "test:scripts names 7 suite(s)" and "every suite in the alias has a step in this job"; the workflow still parses (validate 21 steps, e2e-typecheck 4, e2e 14); repo:validate passes. NOT RUN, AND WHY: the test:scripts alias as a whole does not complete -- scripts/test-ai-control-plane.mjs hangs, which is PL-0735, filed P0 this round after being found by this very command. That hang predates this task, reproduces on a clean worktree of 1474d0b, and is why CI validate has been in progress for over an hour on runs 181 and 182. The six pre-existing suites in the alias are therefore unverified by me today; the one this task adds is verified directly.
